title: Maintenance plans and inspections
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-6 met: the next due date is last done plus the frequency in its unit and is never stored; an inspection with findings cannot close without a correctly linked corrective action; a generated job records the plan it came from and the date it was generated; the compliance state is derived from the computed date; a frequency always carries its unit and a unit never stands alone; and every recorded change names its actor and date.

dataModel.owner: The plan record is the owner's WELL_MAINTENANCE_PLAN in DevelopmentPlanning, the inspections are PPDM's WORK_ORDER_INSPECTION, and the generated jobs are WELL_SERVICE_JOB. The stage's open question - which project owns the plan record - is answered by keeping it where the owner already keeps it and adding only the schedule.
dataModel.additive: WELL_MAINTENANCE_PLAN already carried the asset, type, status, priority and a planned window but no frequency at all, so FREQUENCY, FREQUENCY_UNIT, LAST_DONE_DATE, TASK_LIST and the edit actor/date were added on its own partial class. WELL_SERVICE_JOB had no link back to the plan, so MAINT_PLAN_ID and GENERATED_ON were added the same way. Next due and compliance are computed, never columns.
dataModel.link: An inspection's linked action is the corrective-action PROJECT reachable through the work order's WORK_ORDER_COMPONENT.PROJECT_ID - the same link HSE-03 and WRK-02 use, so no second action table was invented.

rules.nextDue: NextDue(lastDone, frequency, unit) adds the frequency in DAY, WEEK (x7), MONTH or YEAR; a missing frequency, unit or last done returns null rather than a date invented from today.
rules.compliance: Compliance(nextDue, isScheduled, asOf) is 'overdue' before today, 'due' on the day, 'current' after it and 'not scheduled' when the plan has no schedule; days overdue are computed for the chip.
rules.frequency: A frequency requires its unit and a unit requires a positive frequency; both must use one of DAY, WEEK, MONTH or YEAR, and anything else is refused with the list.
rules.generation: GenerateJobAsync refuses a plan that is current or not scheduled, naming its next due date, and records MAINT_PLAN_ID and GENERATED_ON on the job with the planned start at the due date.
rules.closure: An inspection whose notes record findings (or whose result is FAIL) cannot be recorded as closed unless the work order has a corrective action linked; a clean result is recorded directly.
rules.actor: Every write records its actor and its timestamp: the plan's schedule edit, the job's creator and generation date, and the inspection's inspector and inspected-at.

implementation.owner: Beep.OilandGas.DevelopmentPlanning/Data/Tables/WELL_MAINTENANCE_PLAN.Schedule.cs and WELL_SERVICE_JOB.Generation.cs (additive partials; both classes were already partial)
implementation.service: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Data/Work/OgMaintenance.cs (OgMaintenancePlan, OgServiceJob, OgInspectionRow, OgMaintenanceWorkspace, WorkMaintenanceRules, IOgMaintenance, OgMaintenanceService with LoadAsync/EditPlanAsync/GenerateJobAsync/RecordInspectionAsync)
implementation.page: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/MaintenancePageView.cs (route 'maintenance': the asset filter, the counts, the plan grid with its schedule editor and the generate command, the job grid, the inspection grid with its result bar)
implementation.wiring: OgBootstrapper (IOgMaintenance), OgApplication.Maintenance, catalog 'maintenance' (OgModuleKeys.Work), OgPageFactory, en + ar labels
implementation.tests: test/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Tests/MaintenancePlanTests.cs (6, no database) + MaintenanceGatewayTests.cs (1 opt-in, real SQLite over six tables)

integration.database: SQLite with WELL_MAINTENANCE_PLAN, WELL_SERVICE_JOB, WORK_ORDER_INSPECTION, WORK_ORDER, WORK_ORDER_COMPONENT and PROJECT. One plan on UWI-1 every 30 days last done 2026-10-01, one work order with one close-out inspection, and a corrective-action project that can be linked.
integration.ac1_nextDue: the plan's next due reads 2026-10-31 from last done plus 30 days, and the state is overdue against 2026-11-08 with the days overdue in the text
integration.ac5_unit: saving 7 without a unit is refused with maintenance-frequency-unit-required and the stored frequency stays 30
integration.ac3_job: generating from the overdue plan writes a job with MAINT_PLAN_ID 'PLAN-1', GENERATED_ON 2026-11-08 and the actor; after rescheduling to every 7 days from 2026-11-05 the plan is current and generation is refused with maintenance-not-due
integration.ac2_findings: recording a FAIL with findings is refused with maintenance-findings-need-action until a corrective-action project is linked to the work order; a clean PASS is recorded with its inspector and timestamp
integration.ac4_compliance: compliance is recomputed on every read from the computed date; nothing is stored
integration.ac6_actor: the plan edit records SCHEDULE_EDITED_BY, the job records its creator and generation date, and the inspection records its inspector and inspected-at
integration.failure: a service without a connection returns no workspace, and the page's failed branch clears all three grids

gates.AC-1 Next due is last done plus frequenc: pass - computed for DAY, WEEK, MONTH and YEAR and null without a schedule.
gates.AC-2 An inspection with findings cannot: pass - refused with the reason, then allowed once a corrective action is linked to the work order.
gates.AC-3 A generated job references its plan: pass - both columns written and asserted in SQL.
gates.AC-4 Compliance state is derived, not st: pass - computed on every read from the computed due date.
gates.AC-5 Frequency always carries a unit: pass - a frequency without a unit, a unit without a frequency and an unknown unit are all refused.
gates.AC-6 Every recorded action names its act: pass - the plan edit, the generated job and the inspection all record both.

planRecordHadNoFrequency.finding: The owner's plan records the asset, maintenance type, status, priority and a planned window - and no frequency, unit, last done or tasks, so 'next due' had no recorded source.
planRecordHadNoFrequency.handling: The schedule is added on the plan's own partial class; the owner's columns are untouched, and a plan without a schedule reads 'not scheduled' rather than being given one.

jobHadNoPlanLink.finding: WELL_SERVICE_JOB records the asset and a job status but nothing that says which plan produced it.
jobHadNoPlanLink.handling: MAINT_PLAN_ID and GENERATED_ON are additive columns; a job raised by hand simply has no plan id.

inspectionHasNoDueDate.finding: WORK_ORDER_INSPECTION records the result, the notes, the inspector and when it was inspected, but no due date - the due date belongs to the work order.
inspectionHasNoDueDate.handling: The inspection's due date is the linked WORK_ORDER.DUE_DATE, and an inspection with no work order shows none.

requiredInspectionColumns.finding: WORK_ORDER_INSPECTION marks JURISDICTION and REQUIREMENT_ACTOR required, so an update of a seeded row without them fails validation.
requiredInspectionColumns.handling: The update preserves the recorded values and the gateway test seeds them; a real inspection always has them because the owner's write path sets them.

generationDateFormat.finding: A date-only predicate on GENERATED_ON matched nothing because the provider stores a datetime.
generationDateFormat.handling: The test compares with a date prefix; the stored value is a date at midnight.

limits: The plan's tasks are a free-text list, not structured task rows with their own skills and materials as the feature's editor describes; there is no task table in the owner's schema.
There is no frequency tolerance window: the feature mentions one, but nothing in the owner's records defines it, so none is invented and a plan is due on its due date.
An inspection's 'findings' are its RESULT_NOTES text; the owner records no finding rows, so a finding cannot be individually tracked.

The linked action is a corrective-action project reached through the work order component; the desktop does not confirm that the action addresses this inspection's finding, only that one is linked to the work order.
A generated job is a single record with the plan's due date as its planned window; there is no scheduling or resource assignment, which the stage places elsewhere.
The inspection list is filtered by the asset through its work order's component, so an inspection whose work order has no component is not shown for a filtered asset.
No per-command permission enforcement: the page is gated, and work.maintenance.write/generate and work.inspection.write are not checked per command.
The page has one plan editor, one generate command and one inspection bar rather than the Web's recorded-work, evidence, asset-return and closure panels; those panels are deferred.
